rationale: This is essentially the archive's "Reported Earnings Accrual Reliance Trap" with a one-year difference applied to the reliance ratio, a cosmetic level-to-change variant whose DELTA of a ratio with a volatile, sign-unstable |ib|+|oancf| denominator adds mostly noise rather than new economics.

target_name: Book Value Clean Earnings Deficit Trap
rationale: The construction is internally consistent (cheap book equity plus negative three-year clean earnings yields high scores, matching the negative expected sign) and meaningfully differs from the archive's denominator-penalty version by targeting the short side, though much of the predictive content may come from the standalone cumulative-profitability leg rather than the interaction.

This recombines two already-tested archive components — the EV-floored EBITDA yield and the |ebitda|-scaled working-capital reliance share of "Working Capital Share Adjusted EBITDA Yield" — into a multiplicative trap, making it an incremental re-parameterization of a tested idea rather than a substantively new mechanism.

The recch sign convention is handled correctly and the cheap-revenue-with-uncollected-sales trap is coherently specified, but the receivable-accrual leg is close to a known Sloan-style earnings-quality anomaly and recch's ~8% coverage in this archive limits how much new evidence it can generate.

This is structurally the same expression as the receivable proposal with sale substituted for the near-identical revt and invch for recch, so it is a within-batch near-duplicate whose accrual leg largely rediscovers the published inventory-growth anomaly.

The signed depreciation shortfall relative to the firm's own recent policy is the least crowded content in this archive and the trap construction is directionally consistent, though it reuses the same rank-times-reliance template and overlaps in spirit with the already-tested "Depreciation Normalized Earnings Yield".
